en: Dependent on a state that is non-conflict (*araṇa*), non-demonstrable (*anidassana*), and impinging (*sappaṭigha*), there arises a state that is non-refuge (*nasaraṇa*), non-demonstrable, and impinging, by way of root condition. (In all cases, one.

Dependent on a state that is with-refuge (*saraṇa*), non-demonstrable, and non-impinging (*appaṭigha*), there arises a state that is non-refuge, non-demonstrable, and non-impinging, by way of root condition.
Dependent on a state that is non-conflict, non-demonstrable, and non-impinging... [there arises] a state that is non-refuge, non-demonstrable, and non-impinging... by way of root condition.

A state arises by way of root condition. Dependent on a state that is with-conflict (saraṇa) and non-demonstrable-non-reactive (anidassana-appaṭigha), as well as a state that is without-conflict (araṇa) and non-demonstrable-non-reactive, a state that is neither-with-conflict-nor-non-demonstrable-non-reactive arises by way of root condition.
There are three [answers] for root; one for mutuality … pe … one for result … pe … three for non-disappearance.

Dependent on a state that is neither a cause nor an object—non-conflictual (*araṇa*), non-demonstrable, and non-reactive—a state that is neither a refuge nor non-demonstrable/non-reactive arises by way of the root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*).

Dependent on a state that is a refuge, non-demonstrable, and non-reactive, a state that is neither a refuge nor non-demonstrable/non-reactive arises by way of the object-condition (*ārammaṇa-paccaya*). (Abbreviated.)

By way of not-root: one; by way of not-object: three …pe… by way of not-kamma: one …pe… by way of not-nutriment, not-faculty, not-jhāna, and not-path: one …pe… by way of not-dissociation: one …pe… by way of not-disappearance: three.
(The “Conascent” section …pe… and the “Associated” section are also similar to the “Dependent” section.
A state that is with-conflict, non-visible, and non-reactive is, by way of root-condition, a condition for a state that is without-conflict, non-visible, and non-reactive.

A state that is non-conflictual (*araṇa*), non-demonstrable (*anidassana*), and non-reactive (*appaṭigha*) is a condition, by way of the root-condition (*hetu-paccaya*), for a state that is not non-conflictual, not non-demonstrable, and not non-reactive.

(Abbreviated. Under root-cause: two; predominance: two; conascence, dependence: three; post-nascence, kamma: two; result: one; nutriment, faculty, jhāna, path, dissociation: two ... pe ... non-disappearance: three.

A refugeless, non-demonstrable, and non-reactive state is a condition for a refugeless, non-demonstrable, and non-reactive state by way of co-nascence condition, post-nascence condition, and kamma condition. (Abbreviated.
There are three [answers] for "not-root," three for "not-object," ... pe ... three for "not-non-disappearance.
(It should be expanded in detail just as the section on questions in the Wholesome Triplet.)
